## What's Changed

### Security fixes

2.14.0 fixes three vulnerabilities reported privately against v2. Upgrade with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest`. One of them, GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937, also affects the deprecated v1 line, where it is fixed in 1.0.4 (`@v1-latest`).

* **An MCP App can no longer navigate its sandbox frame away from the policy it was given.** The proxy enforces a frame policy built from the app's approved CSP grants. When the frame starts to leave the document the host loaded, it closes the relay and removes the frame, and it tells the host why. ([GHSA-h9j8-vj8g-v3gg](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-h9j8-vj8g-v3gg))
* **server.json import shows the exact command before it is saved**, and rejects a package with an invalid or empty environment-variable name or unsafe tokens. **URL elicitations open only http(s) URLs.** Any other scheme is refused, with a reason. **The HTML preview's CSP now precedes all document markup.** ([GHSA-rwv7-mh2c-ff2p](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-rwv7-mh2c-ff2p))
* **Server-supplied schema patterns are checked in bounded time.** Tool output and app elicitation schemas use a linear-time matcher with per-pattern and per-schema limits. A pattern beyond those limits is reported as unverified instead of being evaluated. ([GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937))

### Upgrading

* **The Node floor is now `^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`**, the October 2026 Node security releases (#2822). npm prints `EBADENGINE` on older versions. The field is advisory, so the Inspector still runs.
* **`--load` latency now counts successful calls only.** `latencyMs` and the `--load-max-p99` gate cover successful calls only, failed calls are reported separately as `errorLatencyMs`, and tool-error text is now shown (#2836). If no call succeeds, `--load-max-p99` fails with a message saying there is no p99 to check.

## What's Changed

### v1.x security fixes

1.0.4 is a security release for the deprecated v1 line. Upgrade with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@v1-latest`, or move to v2 (`@latest`).

* **Server-supplied `pattern` regexes are no longer evaluated.** Patterns in a tool's output schema and in an elicitation's requested schema are stripped before validation, including patterns reachable through `$ref`, and the elicitation form no longer passes them to the browser's own field validation. The result says which checks were skipped. A schema the Inspector cannot transform safely, such as one that declares `$id` or anchors, is reported as not validated instead of being evaluated. Because patterns are no longer evaluated, a value that fails a server's `pattern` is now accepted, with that note. Every other schema constraint still applies. ([GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-2fw8-7jmw-r937))
* chore(release): bump version to 1.0.4 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/2884

## Security: Node.js runtime advisories (October 2026)

On October 20, 2026, eMudhra disclosed that the private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates could be recovered from the public certificates. On October 21, Node.js shipped [security releases](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases) that update its bundled CA certificates for the compromise. The same releases fix several unrelated high-severity runtime CVEs, including DNS name truncation, TLS hostname checks on non-canonical IP addresses, and an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder.

**How this release stands**

- **The Inspector relies on the Node.js runtime for certificate checks.** It ships no CA certificates of its own and doesn't opt into the system trust store. Every HTTPS connection it makes, to MCP servers and to OAuth discovery and token endpoints, is verified by the Node.js it runs on.
- **The Docker image needs no action.** `ghcr.io/modelcontextprotocol/inspector:2.13.0` runs Node.js **22.23.4**, a patched release, and contains no system CA store.
- **This release also updates two of its own dependencies past published advisories:** `undici` (#2812) and `fast-uri` (#2820).

**If you run the Inspector from npm (`npx` or a global install)**

It runs on your Node.js, which we can't update for you. Please run Node.js **22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or later**, and check with `node --version`. The package's `engines` field still accepts Node.js 22.19.0 and up, so npm won't warn you about an older, unpatched runtime. Node.js 20 and earlier are end-of-life, get no fix, and aren't supported by Inspector v2.

## What's Changed

### Security fixes

2.12.0 fixes three vulnerabilities that affect every v2 release from 2.0.0 through 2.11.0. Upgrade with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@latest`.

* **Opening a URL is restricted to `http(s)`, and the Inspector opens the URL it checked rather than the raw input.** A remote server's OAuth authorization URL can no longer run commands through the opener on Windows and WSL. `open` is bumped to v11 ([GHSA-q978-78c7-phqw](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-q978-78c7-phqw))
* **The production web server validates the `Host` header** and answers any host outside its allow-list with 403 before serving a page. That closes the DNS-rebinding route to the API token and stored OAuth tokens. A new `MCP_INSPECTOR_ALLOWED_HOSTS` covers reverse proxies that rewrite `Host` ([GHSA-vcc9-3xgm-p9v4](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-vcc9-3xgm-p9v4))
* **The `/api/fetch` proxy caps upstream response bodies at 4 MiB**, refusing early when `Content-Length` declares more, and still relays the status of an oversized error response ([GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/security/advisories/GHSA-m5pj-3536-3xcp))

* fix(mcpdo): give resources/directory/read a URI and a cursor by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/2775

* chore(release): merge v2/main into main for v2.12.0 by @cliffhall in https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/pull/2769


### New configuration

* `MCP_INSPECTOR_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: unset by default. Comma-separated extra hostnames the prod web server accepts in `Host`. A leading `.` admits a domain and its subdomains. See the web README's "The Host allow-list" section.
* `INSPECTOR_TLS_KEY_PATH` and `INSPECTOR_TLS_CERT_PATH`: unset by default. Set both to serve the web UI over https, in both prod and dev. See [`docs/tls.md`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/blob/main/docs/tls.md).
